{{Use list-defined references|date=February 2022}}
'''Matilde Noemí Lalín''' is an Argentine-Canadian mathematician specializing in [[number theory]] and known for her work on [[L-function]]s, [[Mahler measure]], and their connections. She is a professor of mathematics at the [[Université de Montréal]].{{r|lathisms|knp}}

==Education and career==
Lalín is originally from [[Buenos Aires]],{{r|lathisms|cv}} and is a [[dual citizen]] of Argentina and Canada.{{r|cv}} As a high school student, she represented Argentina twice in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], in 1993 and 1995, earning a silver medal in 1995.{{r|imo}}

She earned a [[licenciatura]] in 1999 from the [[University of Buenos Aires]].{{r|lathisms|cv}} After starting graduate study at [[Princeton University]] and spending a term as a visiting student at [[Harvard University]], she completed her doctorate in 2005 at the [[University of Texas at Austin]].{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Some Relations of Mahler Measure with Hyperbolic Volumes and Special Values of L-Functions'', was supervised there by Fernando Rodriguez-Villegas.{{r|mg}}

She became a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]], [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]], [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]], and [[Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences]], before obtaining a tenure-track faculty position in 2007 as an assistant professor of mathematics at the [[University of Alberta]]. She moved to the Université de Montréal in 2010, earned tenure as an associate professor there in 2012, and was promoted to full professor in 2018.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Lalín is the 2022 winner of the [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]] of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]], "for her outstanding contributions to research in Number Theory and related areas".{{r|knp}} She was named to the 2023 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]], "for contributions to number theory, including the study of L-functions, and for service to the mathematical community".{{r|fams}} In 2024, she will become a fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], "For her ongoing contributions to the AWM, most notably her leadership role in the Women in Numbers Network and considerable contributions to its growth; her service to the International Mathematics Union Committee for Women; and for her ardent efforts towards making conferences more welcoming and accessible for researchers by actively advocating for childcare resources."<ref>{{Cite web|title=2024 Class of AWM Fellows|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2024-awm-fellows/}}</ref>
